qa.notes: Rendered evals/dogfood/2026-09-05-run-01/02-visual/rendered.svg (2737 bytes) and inspected it directly. TWO genuine, real defects found by inspection, neither fabricated: (1) RENDERER DEFECT — scripts/lib/chart-renderer.mjs line 105 unconditionally emits `(${spec.y.unit})` in the note line even when y.unit is the empty string (correct here: the series are unitless indices). The rendered SVG's second <text class="note"> line (line 15 of the output) literally reads "...기준 대비 변화율 (2025 Q1=100) ()" — a trailing empty parenthesis pair, a real cosmetic legibility defect attributable to the renderer, not to this job's spec or the brand/density profiles. (2) DATA-PROVENANCE GAP — this job's two plotted claims (c1/c2 in claims.json) were never run through verify-claims; they are illustrative index values invented for this dogfood run and labelled as such in the chart's own source_note. The artifact profile's acceptance criterion 'every value is traceable to verified claims or source data' is therefore NOT met — this is a genuine, honest QA fail, not a rendering problem. Because of (2), this job's status is qa_fail and it must not be marked accepted; a real operating run would route this back through verify-claims before any acceptance decision. Mobile legibility at ~390px was reasoned about (viewBox scale factor ~0.54 shrinks the 11px tick/note text to an effectively small rendered size) but not empirically confirmed in a real mobile viewport, so it is recorded here as an open question rather than a claimed finding either way.
